name: awesome-system-design
desc: A curated list of awesome System Design (A.K.A. Distributed Systems) resources.

resources.name: System Design Primer
resources.desc: [109k ⭐] - Awesome compilation of resources, including Anki flashcard decks.

resources.name: System Design Interview Questions - Concepts you should know
resources.desc: A curated list of topics to introduce you to system design.

resources.name: Grokking the System Design Interview
resources.desc: [Paid 💵] - Grokking System Design preparation is one of the most talked about course. The best thing about it is the design of applications it suggests rather than explanations of what each tool is supposed to do.

resources.name: System Design in Software Development
resources.desc: Basic article on the topics of system design and architecture.

resources.name: System Design
resources.desc: Introductory interview preparation resources.

resources.name: Design Pattern for Distributed Systems
resources.desc: Article talking about some patterns as well as some technologies to be considered.

resources.name: Practice system design problems using AI on Codemia.io
resources.desc: A tool which allows you to practice system design problems interactively like an interview with AI. There's iterative feedback and final evaluation which scores your performance

resources.name: Distributed Computing
resources.desc: Wikipedia article broadening the view of distributed system design.

resources.name: Fallacies of Distributed Computing
resources.desc: Wikipedia article introducing the topic of fallacies of distributed computing and its effects.

resources.name: Fallacies of Distributed Computing Explained
resources.desc: In depth explanation of the fallacies mentioned above.

resources.name: CAP Theorem
resources.desc: IBM Article about CAP Theorem, Microservices and NoSQL DBs.

resources.name: Pattern: Microservice Architecture
resources.desc: Good article talking about Microservice architecture as well as its drawbacks.

resources.name: Taxonomy of Distributed Systems
resources.desc: 11 Page lecture classifying distributed systems and specifically why we need them.

resources.name: Top 10 Secure Coding Practices
resources.desc: Brief article talking about good practices for code securities.

resources.name: Scalable Web Architecture and Distributed Systems
resources.desc: Good article about distributed systems as well as some of the potential tools.

resources.name: Designing Distributed Systems: Patterns and Paradigms for Scalable, Reliable Services
resources.desc: [Paid 💵] - Book that talks about disitributed systems as well as lightly demonstrating some code of what it looks like.

resources.name: Designing Data Intensive Applications
resources.desc: [Paid 💵] - Goes in depth to explain various resources we use when working with distributed systems, as well as how it came to be and what problems it aims to solve.

resources.name: The System Design Manual
resources.desc: [Paid 💵] - Covers the core aspects of distributed systems, like: network fundamentals, the theory underpinning distributed systems, architectural patterns of scalable systems, stability patterns that harden systems against failures and operational best-practices on how to maintain large-scale systems with a small team.

resources.name: Building Microservices
resources.desc: [Free 👍] - Awesome book that talks about designing sytem architecture with microservices in depth, includes most relevant topics in this regard.

resources.name: Monolith to Microservices
resources.desc: [Free 👍] - Written by the same author as the one above, this book will cover the migration from Monolith to Microservices, it's recommended you start by the previous book.

resources.name: Distributed Systems (3rd Edition)
resources.desc: [Free 👍] - Great overview of and in-depth introduction to distributed systems. Recommended for intermediate level readers.

resources.name: Safe by Design
resources.desc: [Free 👍] - Great book on enforcing code correctness by design.

resources.name: Gaurav Sen - System Design Series
resources.desc: Good resource for people who want to learn more about system design, introduces the topic in a very easy to understand way.

resources.name: Tech Dummies - System Design Series
resources.desc: Another introduction to system design.

resources.name: Mock System Design Interview at Google
resources.desc: Overview of what an interview on system design would look like from the perspective of a flawed but close fulfilling of the requirements. Key thing here is how the interaction with the interviewer goes.

resources.name: Google Preparation Guide
resources.desc: A quick video explaining how they interview.

resources.name: System Design Interview
resources.desc: YouTube channel focussed on content specific to system design interviews, with detailed explanation of a variety of problems.

resources.name: Intro to Architecture and System Design Interviews
resources.desc: A youtube video with Jackson Gabbard with good info about system design interviews.

resources.name: System Design Introduction for Interview
resources.desc: Tushar's intro to System Design.

resources.name: Distributed Systems
resources.desc: This is an introductory course in Distributed Systems made by Chris Colohan. He got PhD from Carnegie Mellon, then spent 10 years working at Google building distributed systems.

resources.name: The Easy Way
resources.desc: Up and coming channel with easy to understand videos about Distributed Systems.

resources.name: System Design by SDE Skills
resources.desc: Good resource for people who are preparing for System Design interviews, there are multiple system design mock interviews and deep dives.

resources.name: System Design by CodeKarle
resources.desc: Another great free resource, a list of commonly asked interview questions.

resources.name: The evolution of Reddit Architecture
resources.desc: Overview of how Reddit system design scaled.

resources.name: 6.824 Distributed Systems by MIT
resources.desc: Graduate level course on distributed systems from MIT (2020).

resources.name: CSE138 Distributed Systems by UCSC
resources.desc: Undergraduate course on distributed systems from UCSC (2020).

resources.name: MariaDB
resources.desc: MariaDB is a fork of MySQL server.

resources.name: MySQL
resources.desc: Widely used relational database.

resources.name: PostgresSQL
resources.desc: Relational database that has been gaining popularity.

resources.name: SQLite
resources.desc: Another widely used database that is built into all mobile phones and most computers.

resources.name: Sql Server
resources.desc: Widely used relational database.

resources.name: Apache Ignite
resources.desc: [3.3k ⭐] - In memory caching with ACID properties.

resources.name: Couchbase
resources.desc: Inspired by memcached, adding features such as replication and persistance.

resources.name: Oracle Coherence
resources.desc: [126 ⭐] - High scaling, low latency in-memory caching.

resources.name: Memcached
resources.desc: [10.2k ⭐] - One of the first in-memory caching database, high performing and multi-threaded.

resources.name: Redis
resources.desc: [44k ⭐] - Widely used in-memory caching database with many added features such as persistent storage and supporting strings, lists, sets, hashses, streams, bitmaps, etc.

resources.name: Apple FoundationDB
resources.desc: [10k ⭐] - Multi-model (many data types in a single database), ACID key-value store. Easily scalable and fault tolerant.

resources.name: Cosmos DB
resources.desc: Microsoft's globally distributed, multi-model database service. Eastically and independently scale throughput and storage. SQL, MongoDB, Cassandra, Tables, Gremlin, and Spark APIs.

resources.name: CouchDB
resources.desc: [4.6k ⭐] - ACID compliant NoSQL document-store DB, provides a RESTful HTTP API for reading and updating database documents.

resources.name: MongoDB
resources.desc: One of the most popular 'NoSQL' database for general purpose.

resources.name: RethinkDB
resources.desc: [23.8k ⭐] - Document-store DB.

resources.name: ElasticSearch
resources.desc: [49.9k ⭐] - Widely popular 'NoSQL' database for fast and scalable search engines.

resources.name: Amazon DynamoDB
resources.desc: Key-Value and Document database, highly performant, scalable and secure.

resources.name: Google Bigtable
resources.desc: Scalable and performant 'NoSQL' database for large analytical and operational workload.

resources.name: Cassandra
resources.desc: Facebook-born project very fast, easily scalable, with option to include consistency with each operation.

resources.name: Scylla
resources.desc: [4.9k ⭐] - 'NoSQL' data store using seastar framework, compatible with Cassandra.

resources.name: HBase
resources.desc: [3.6k ⭐] - Modeled after Google's Bigtable and written in Java. Developed as a part of Apache Hadoop project and runs on top of HDFS or Alluxio. (See Hadoop Related)

resources.name: Amazon Neptune
resources.desc: Fast, reliable and fully managed graph database service.

resources.name: ArangoDB
resources.desc: [10k ⭐] - Flexible database for documents, key-value, graphs. Uses its own query language, AQL.

resources.name: Neo4j
resources.desc: [7.9k ⭐] - Good support for a graph db, ACID compliant and flexible.

resources.name: HDFS
resources.desc: Hadoop File System is a a widely popular choice among its big data competitors, providing high throughput access.

resources.name: Lustre
resources.desc: File system for computer clusters.

resources.name: CephFS
resources.desc: Unified, distributed storage system.

resources.name: GlusterFS
resources.desc: Scale-out NAS file system.

resources.name: MooseFS
resources.desc: POSIX-compliant distributed file system.

resources.name: XtreemFS
resources.desc: Fault tolerant file system.

resources.name: Kubernetes
resources.desc: Highly popular way to deploy, manage and automatically scale a cluster of containers on bare-metal or virtual servers.

resources.name: Apache Samza
resources.desc: Build stateful applications that process data in real time from multiple sources, including Kafka. Easy and inexpensive multi-subscriber model, can eliminate backpressure and has reliable persistency with low latency.

resources.name: Apache Flink
resources.desc: Based on the concept of streams and transofrmations. Uses maven, handles batch tasks as data streams with finite boundaries. Low latency, high throughput.

resources.name: Amazon Kinesis Streams
resources.desc: Durable, scalable, real-tme service. Collects gigabytes of data per second from hundreds of thousands of sources, including database event streams, website clickstreams, financial transactions, etc.

resources.name: Azure Stream Analytics
resources.desc: Real-time analytics service that is designed for mission-critical workloads.

resources.name: Amazon MQ
resources.desc: Open source message broker from Amazon.

resources.name: Apache ActiveMQ
resources.desc: It's a multi-protocol, java based messaging server.

resources.name: Apache Kafka
resources.desc: Widely popular message broker with low latency for data streaming.

resources.name: RabbitMQ
resources.desc: Widely popular lightweight

resources.name: IronMQ
resources.desc: Very fast and highly scalable messaging broker. (not open source)

resources.name: Apache Pulsar
resources.desc: Created by yahoo, also highly scalable, low latency, geo-replication and multi-tenacy.

resources.name: Kestrel
resources.desc: Written in Scala and speaks the memcached protocol. It works much like Kafka.

resources.name: Azure Service Bus
resources.desc: A fully managed enterprise integration message broker.

resources.name: SeeSaw
resources.desc: [5.1k ⭐] - Used by Google, developed in Go, linux-based virtual load balancer server.

resources.name: HAProxy
resources.desc: Widely popular option, provides high-availability, proxy, TCP/HTTP load balancing. Used by Reddit, Imgur, MaxCDN, GitHub, AirBNB.

resources.name: Zevenet
resources.desc: Supports L3, L4 and L7. Easy install with a docker repo. Supports advanced health-check monitorining.

resources.name: Neutrino
resources.desc: Used by eBay, built with Scala and Netty. Supports round-robin and least-connection algorithms.

resources.name: Nginx
resources.desc: Wait, isn't Nginx a web server? Yes, the open source does support basic level of content switching and request routing. Plus edition supports load balancing, WAF, monitoring, etc.

resources.name: Openresty
resources.desc: Nginx + Lua, perfect combination.

resources.name: F5
resources.desc: Robust hardware load balancer option, supporting multiple protocols (IP, TCP, FTP, UDP, HTTP).

resources.name: TP-Link
resources.desc: Cheaper alternative that works as a load balancer.

resources.name: Barracuda
resources.desc: One of the top choices for load balancing when it comes to in-house servers. Top security measures built in, comprehensive reports and monitoring outbound traffic for data loss prevention.

resources.name: Amazon Elastic Load Balancing
resources.desc: Popular choice for amazon customers, supports lambda functions, highly scalable.

resources.name: Google Load Balancing
resources.desc: Popular choice for google customers, comes with auto-scaling feature, very fast, has intergrated CDN.

resources.name: Cloudflare Load Balancing
resources.desc: Scalable load balancing by Cloudflare, feature fast failover and a dashboard.

resources.name: DigitalOcean Load Balancing
resources.desc: If you're a digitalocean customer, this is a good option, very cheap, regional availability, scalable, easy to deploy among your other droplets.

resources.name: Azure Load Balancing
resources.desc: Popular choice for Microsoft's Azure customers. Supports internal and external traffics, ipv6, monitorining and the standard load balancing set of features.

resources.name: Ambari
resources.desc: Dashboard that integrates most of hadoop related technologies for easy management and executions.

resources.name: Sqoop
resources.desc: Efficiently transfer data between Hadoop and structured datastores such as relational databases.

resources.name: Flume
resources.desc: Distributed, highly available and efficient in collecting, aggregating and moving large amounts of log data.

resources.name: Oozie
resources.desc: Create workflows in xml to execute jobs (from other hadoop-ecosystem applications) in steps, allows for parallel execution as well.

resources.name: Hive
resources.desc: Query hadoop stored data in SQL.

resources.name: Pig
resources.desc: Scriping language that looks like SQL to query hadoop data.

resources.name: Tez
resources.desc: Solves a similar problem to Spark and MapReduce, it's more efficient than MapReduce because it calculates the most efficient way of doing it.

resources.name: Map Reduce
resources.desc: MapReduce, as the name implies, maps data and reduce the results.

resources.name: Spark
resources.desc: Powerful data processing to not only process data like Tez (and MapReduce), it can process streams of data in real time, apply regression analysis algorithms in ML and much more.

resources.name: Apex
resources.desc: \*Retired project, it's a YARN-native platform that unifies stream and batch processing.

resources.name: YARN
resources.desc: 'Yet Another Resource Negotiator', works like a kernel to manage computer resources across the clusters.

resources.name: MESOS
resources.desc: Works like a Linux Kernel by managing CPU, memory, storage and other resources across the cluster.

resources.name: Gin
resources.desc: [40.6k ⭐] - Blazingly fast microservice framework using Golang, high throughput capacity.

resources.name: Phoenix
resources.desc: [15.5k ⭐] - Distributed processing, easily scalable, support for channels and live chat. This framework - written in Elixir, uses BEAM and Erlang, very efficient for large scale systems and supports high throughput.

resources.name: Express.js
resources.desc: [49.6k ⭐] - Fast node.js rest api that can perform well under many scenarios.

resources.name: Rails
resources.desc: [46.2k ⭐] - Written in Ruby, Rails delivers quick apis from prototype to production in an efficient manner.

resources.name: Play Framework
resources.desc: [11.6k ⭐] - Very fast, high throughput framework written in Scala/Java that is RESTful by default.

resources.name: Flask
resources.desc: [51.6k ⭐] - A lightweight Python Microframework for fast prototyping and production.

resources.name: FastAPI
resources.desc: [22.7k ⭐] - A lightweight Python Microframework inspired in Flask but more modern, using Python async.

resources.name: Django REST
resources.desc: [18.4k ⭐] - Written in Python, Django Rest is a powerful and flexible REST API. The efficiency and time to market resembles Rails.

resources.name: ASP.NET Core MVC
resources.desc: A rich framework for building web apps and APIs using the Model-View-Controller design pattern in C# or F#. Number 6 on TechEmpower Composite Benchmarks for web frameworks.

resources.name: Fastify
resources.desc: [15.4k ⭐] - A Node.js web framework highly focused on providing the best developer experience with the least overhead and a powerful plugin architecture.
